subject: res-network-ports-and-listeners
text:
- **Network ports and listeners:** no network port — no TCP or UDP port; one local listener — the driver session's Unix-domain socket `{state_dir}/session.sock`, set to mode `0600` inside a state directory the caller names and `escher_driver::serve` creates `0700`, bound at the tree's one served listener site (beside it, since 2026-10-14-quality-gates, one test-only bind: escher-driver's unix-only unit test `client::imp::tests::an_answer_read_past_its_bound_is_a_timeout` binds a `UnixListener` in `eab-{pid}` under the system temporary directory, accepts one connection and never answers, then removes the directory — no binary serves it and no caller reaches it, so it is no crossing, the operator's answer at that chunk's wrap, 2026-10-15; packages/escher-driver/src/client.rs:263-308), serving three requests at wire version `v3`, a call's replies including the fixed `recording-failed` — `hello`, `stop` and, since 2026-10-10-driver-cli, `call` — so a call's element id and typed text cross in and an answer's ids, accessible names, control values (a password's or a file input's as the fixed mask), snapshot text and diff cross out, no `NodeId` among them, a request line at most 16,384 bytes and an answer at most 1,048,576; still no second listener; unix only — on other targets the lifecycle and a call return `SessionError::Unsupported` in 0.1.0 (packages/escher-driver/src/host.rs:109-124; packages/escher-driver/src/wire.rs:12) — a boundary widening, the founder's choice (the founder, 2026-10-07, relayed verbatim), as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-07-driver-session/report.md, and widened again from lifecycle messages only to calls and their answers, ratified by the founder (2026-10-10, by question dialog in the overseer session, relayed verbatim by the overseer as his chosen option label «Сокет несёт команды»;
 the English wording is the overseer's), as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-10-driver-cli/report.md. Since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface the `escher-session mcp` role (`escher_driver::serve_mcp`) speaks newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 over its own stdin and stdout to the MCP client that spawned it, local to the invoking user — no listener, socket or port, so the session socket is still the one listener and there is still no network port; a tool call brings an element id and typed text in, and a result takes ids, accessible names, control values (a password's or a file input's as the fixed mask), snapshot text and diff out — a boundary widening ratified by the founder (2026-10-10, «Ратифицировать как есть», by question dialog in the overseer session, relayed verbatim by the overseer as his chosen option label; the English wording is the overseer's), as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-10-mcp-surface/report.md. Since 2026-10-12-self-description the role also serves the `help` tool, answered by the server with no session run, and speaks a fourth handshake revision, `2025-11-25`, now its default; a result also carries the tool's self-description and a session error's remedy, and the tool listing each verb's result fields — the program's own fixed `'static` table text inside the ratified carrier, ratified by the founder (2026-10-12, «Внутри, с правилом», relayed verbatim by the overseer) — and a changed node's `differs`, closed node-key words; still no listener, socket or port, and the session socket unchanged (as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-12-self-description/report.md).
 Since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot both carriers also take a shot of the screen out: the socket's answer to a `screenshot` call holds its PNG as base64 inside the JSON line, and the `mcp` role's result an `image` block (`image/png`, base64) then a text block — screen pixels in band, a boundary widening ratified by the founder (2026-10-12, «В самом ответе», relayed verbatim by the overseer) — still the one listener and no port, the wire's bounds unchanged, an MCP result that holds an image bounded by its whole written form (as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-12-headless-screenshot/report.md). Both carriers, and a kept check, also take a lint's findings out as the `lint` verb's answer — stable ids, the closed defect words and numbers, no `NodeId`, page text, colour or control value — a ratified boundary widening (§Established Decisions → [Driver session]); still the one listener and no port, the wire's bounds unchanged (as measured at escher-0.2.0/chunks/2026-10-19-visual-lint/report-gated.md).
 As adopted, before that chunk, observed absent — network ports or local hosts · searched: `localhost|port` over .github/workflows/*.yml, Cargo.toml, Cross.toml, flake.nix; a listening socket or local port · searched: `TcpListener|localhost|127\.0\.0\.1` over the 32 s03 files; any listening socket or port · searched: `TcpListener|bind\(|listen\(|localhost|127\.0\.0\.1` over the 86 s04 files; network listeners or fixed addresses · searched: `TcpListener|SocketAddr|localhost|127\.0\.0\.1` over the 15 s05 files; network listeners or ports · searched: `TcpListener|localhost|0\.0\.0\.0|\.bind` over the 17 s06 files; ports, sockets or listeners · searched: `port|bind\(|listen` over the 8 s07 files; any network port, socket bind or listener · searched: `fn main|\[\[bin\]\]|clap` over the 16 s08 files; network listeners or fixed host addresses · searched: `TcpListener|UdpSocket|localhost|127\.0\.0\.1` over the 32 s09 files; network listener or port binding · searched: `TcpListener|listen\(` over the 32 s10 files; any network port, host or socket binding · searched: `port|127\.0\.0\.1|localhost` over the 21 s11 files; network ports or listen addresses · searched: `localhost|127\.0\.0\.1|0\.0\.0\.0|bind\(` over the 61 s12 files; a network listener or socket · searched: `TcpListener|TcpStream|bind\(|listen\(` over the 12 s13 files

subject: res-process-wide-state-and-threads
text:

 — since 2026-10-15-cold-agent-test, in place of `python3 cold_agent_stub.py`; the pipe's judge then spawns two `escher-session mcp` replay children directly, without `--record` (stderr to `/dev/null`), one for the full replay of the agent's check and one for the ablated replay, every reply bounded at 30 s (`REPLY_BOUND`), each killed and reaped — that replay crossing on the founder's «Один запуск, до $3 (Рекомендую)» and «JSON-проверка с повтором (Рекомендую)» (2026-10-15, by question dialog in the overseer session, relayed verbatim by the overseer as his chosen option labels; the English wording is the overseer's; confirmed at that chunk's wrap card, «Подтвердить (Рекомендую)»); the run ends them all, no listener, port or socket is added, and the client's own local messaging socket is the client's, opened by no escher code (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-06) (scripts/cold-agent.sh:580-584; scripts/cold-agent.sh:297-336; scripts/cold-agent.sh:339-356; scripts/cold-agent.sh:371-395; as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-06-cold-agent-run-pipe/report.md and escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-15-cold-agent-test/report.md); five blitz-tests integration binaries re-execute their own test binary under `cargo test`, the first three once each and the fourth and fifth twice — since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot `stand_screenshot_repeat` runs `std::env::current_exe()` twice with a fixed argv, each child running its ignored `child_prints_its_shots` and printing its shots to stdout, which the parent captures and reads into its assertions only (tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_screenshot_repeat.rs:75-98;
 tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_screenshot_repeat.rs:139-146), and `telemetry_stdout_silent` runs `std::env::current_exe()` with `--ignored --exact child_emits --nocapture`, its output captured and `RUST_LOG` removed from the child's env, `telemetry_drop` runs it with the same argv, its output captured and `RUST_LOG=warn,style=trace,dioxus_core=trace,selectors=trace` set on the child, which installs the sink with `init`, and `stand_id_persistence` runs it with `--ignored --exact ids_in_a_child_process --nocapture`, its output captured, setting or removing no env var, and `stand_act_spans` runs it with `--ignored --exact {child} --nocapture` on each of its two ignored children, its output captured, `RUST_LOG=info` set on one child and `RUST_LOG` removed from the other, each child installing the sink with `init_with_writer` over an in-memory capture — test-only, a fixed argv, no socket or port (tests/blitz-tests/tests/telemetry_stdout_silent.rs:10-14; tests/blitz-tests/tests/telemetry_drop.rs:14-22; tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_id_persistence.rs:290-300; tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_spans.rs:569-577; as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-06-id-persistence/report.md, `telemetry_drop` at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-07-sink-target-allowlist/report.md, `stand_act_spans` at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-07-driver-command-spans/report.md); two more re-execute it as a session host — `stand_session_lifecycle` on each of its two ignored children, `--ignored --exact session_host --nocapture` serving under `IDLE_EXPIRY` and, since 2026-10-10-driver-cli, `session_host_with_a_short_expiry` serving under a short expiry while the parent watches the state directory go, their streams sent to null, and `stand_session_quiet` with `--ignored --exact session_host_with_typed_text --nocapture`, its streams captured and `RUST_LOG=trace` set on the child
 — each child an `#[ignore]` test that serves one session on its Unix-domain socket in a state directory under `target/tmp/` until it is stopped or idle for its expiry, every wait of the parent bounded and a guard killing and reaping a host a failing check still holds; and eight seven_guis test targets spawn the built `escher-session` binary through `CARGO_BIN_EXE_escher-session` — `host_binary`, and `host_log` on `crud` and on `cells` (its paged part read: a sentinel committed into a part-2 cell, then `snapshot --part 2`; examples/seven_guis/tests/host_log.rs:134-277) with `RUST_LOG=trace`, spawn the host role themselves, both streams piped and drained from the spawn on by one thread of the test process each, the session reached by `attach` polled under a 60 s bound, stopped by `stop` and its exit waited for under a 10 s bound; since 2026-10-10-driver-cli `host_timer` does the same on `timer`, `cli_commands` runs the binary once per command as a client, its sessions started by the binary's own `start` command, as `host_log`'s unix-only recording-clients check does too — `start crud --record` through `stop`, each run at `RUST_LOG=trace`, in `hl-client` and `hl-client-rec`, a `Started` guard stopping the session (examples/seven_guis/tests/host_log.rs:42-132) —

 tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_session_lifecycle.rs:239-255; tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_session_quiet.rs:102-115; examples/seven_guis/tests/host_binary.rs:16; examples/seven_guis/tests/host_log.rs:24; examples/seven_guis/tests/host_log.rs:303-322; examples/seven_guis/tests/common/mod.rs:35-44; as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-07-driver-session/report.md, `host_log` at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-07-sink-target-allowlist/report.md); the `escher-session` host itself is one process holding one session and one listener on its main thread, spawning no thread of its own — serving `load`, the stand's `LoadNet` spawns one per fetch (below) —, started by whoever runs it (`escher_driver::start` spawns the caller's `std::process::Command`) or, since 2026-10-10-driver-cli, by the binary's own `start` command — which spawns the running binary again (`std::env::current_exe()`) as `serve <task> --session <dir>`, with `--record <dir>` after it when it was given one, with stdin, stdout and stderr closed, waits up to 30 s for the host to answer and drops the handle, neither killing nor reaping it — and ended by `stop` or by its idle expiry, 1,800 s with no answered request (examples/seven_guis/src/session_host.rs:8-58; packages/escher-driver/src/cli.rs:456-476); since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface the binary's `mcp` role is one process holding at most one session in process, with no listener and no thread of its own — under a `start load` the stand's `LoadNet` spawns one per fetch; its idle expiry checked when a request arrives — started by the MCP client that spawns it, its stderr the binary's `escher_telemetry::init` sink, a third role reaching that one install site (packages/escher-driver/src/mcp.rs:44-112; packages/escher-driver/src/mcp.rs:140-147)

subject: crosscut-logging-and-timing
text:
- **Logging and timing:** `tracing`, `tracing-subscriber` and `tracing-log` are workspace dependencies (Cargo.toml:188-190); escher binaries install `escher_telemetry::init(escher_telemetry::service_identity!())` at start — today the two binaries of the seven_guis package, which therefore both stamp `service.name=seven_guis`: `seven_guis_native`, unconditionally on the native target, before `dioxus_native::launch`, and the session host `escher-session`, first thing in its native `main`, each reporting an `Err` with `eprintln!` and continuing (examples/seven_guis/src/main.rs:4-10; examples/seven_guis/src/session_host.rs:30-32) — which builds a `Registry` with an `EnvFilter` and one non-ANSI fmt layer using the escher formatter (tracing-subscriber features env-filter · fmt · registry · std · tracing-log) — stated once, in the private `sink_layer`, which since 2026-10-07-driver-command-spans sets `with_span_events(FmtSpan::CLOSE)` and the crate-private field formatter `SpanFields`, so the layer prints a closed span's line beside an event's (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-09 — §Standard Contracts → Telemetry bootstrap) — writes to stderr only, stamps `service.name` / `service.version` on every line, bridges `log` records, drops every record whose target is outside the engine and escher prefix sets (`ENGINE_TARGET_PREFIXES`, `ESCHER_TARGET_PREFIXES`) at every level and whatever `RUST_LOG` names, scrubs the records that print — a closed span's fields by the rule that judges an event's — and chains the panic hook — no filter layer is added, the drop sits in the formatter (packages/escher-telemetry/Cargo.toml:13-16; packages/escher-telemetry/src/lib.rs:102-163; packages/escher-telemetry/src/format.rs:134-178);
 escher-driver emits its command span and, since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface, its `tool_call` span through `tracing` ungated and installs no subscriber (packages/escher-driver/src/execute.rs:96-111); the upstream `tracing_subscriber::fmt::init()` installs run only under the `tracing` feature and write to stdout unscrubbed (apps/browser/src/main.rs:73-74; apps/readme/src/main.rs:76-77; examples/todomvc/src/main.rs:16-17); tracing is an optional feature forwarded down the crate chain (packages/blitz-html/Cargo.toml:15; packages/blitz-net/Cargo.toml:18; packages/blitz-paint/Cargo.toml:15; packages/blitz-shell/Cargo.toml:21; packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/document.rs:256-257; packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/runtime.rs:1104-1105; packages/blitz/src/lib.rs:48-49); the WPT runner uses the `log` facade with `env_logger::init()` (wpt/runner/src/main.rs:26; wpt/runner/src/main.rs:467; wpt/runner/src/net_provider.rs:3); frame and phase time logging are opt-in features `log-frame-times`, `log-phase-times` (Cargo.toml:265-268), resolve phases timed with `debug_timer!` (packages/blitz-dom/src/resolve.rs:77; packages/blitz-dom/src/resolve.rs:169); `screenshot` times phases with a `Timer` printing `"{message} in {diff}ms"` (examples/screenshot.rs:186-215; examples/screenshot.rs:56; examples/screenshot.rs:146); `paint_bench` runs 5 warmup iterations (examples/paint_bench.rs:26; examples/paint_bench.rs:39-50); `multi_doc` times its run and, in its `timed_resolve`, each resolve with `Instant::now()` and prints one summary line on stdout with `println!` (examples/multi_doc.rs:61-67; examples/multi_doc.rs:111-115)

subject: crosscut-invalidation-and-state-integrity
intent
text: - **Front page:** the root `README.md` is escher's own page, not upstream Blitz's — what escher is and, since 2026-10-16-handler-splits-and-readme, its state under `## Status`: 0.1.0 done and verified, its six stages listed with three recorded facts (17 capabilities verified, 43 cold-agent tool calls with 0 wrong, 0 surviving mutants of 1,558), and 0.2.0 planned in five stages, one line per epoch of `escher-0.2.0/working-route.md`, where it read built vs planned; the page spells the name «Escher» in its prose and title, crate, binary and path names, URLs and the e-mail unchanged, on the founder's word «чтоб эшер там с большой буквы писался» (2026-10-16) — and since 2026-10-10-driver-cli how the driver's command line is run (the `escher-session` binary: `start`, one driver command per call answering one line of JSON on stdout, the four exit statuses, `stop`), since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface how an MCP client drives the same apps (it spawns `target/debug/escher-session mcp` as its own child and gets the driver commands as tools, the page saying twelve, the count `VERBS` holds), since 2026-10-12-self-description how to ask for `help` on both surfaces, a link to `docs/capabilities.md` as the statement of what Escher can do and its limits (README.md:48), the screenshot no longer named as still to come since 2026-10-13-upstream-sync-polish-and-ship, its Blitz lineage, the 0.1.0 epochs, the licence and an Author / Contact section, with the fork's `ci.yml` badge as its one image (README.md). No build or doc step reads it, and one test does — the capability-statement pin reads its count of the driver commands as tools (§Standard Contracts → CI contracts); `rdme` resolves a `README.md` at runtime only (apps/readme/src/main.rs:220-233). At an Upstream sync an upstream change to `README.md` resolves to escher's version (upstream touched it 6 times in the 12 months to 2026-10-06, as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-06-project-readme/research.md)
